Hi all,

Attached is Acme's redline to the DPA (file: Acme_DPA_redline_v2.pdf). Headline asks relevant to subprocessors:

- Notice: require 30 days' notice for any new subprocessor who will process Acme personal data.
- Objection window: customer has 15 days to object in writing after receipt of notice.
- Relief: if customer objects and the parties cannot agree within 7 days, Redwood must suspend processing by the contested subprocessor for Acme data and provide written confirmation and remediation steps.
- Audit / evidence: require proof of contracts and SOC 2 evidence for any new subprocessor within 10 business days.

Acme's position is driven by regulatory constraints around health data. We appreciate Redwood's production concerns but need enforceable remedies short of termination.

Please review and advise which points Redwood can accept, which need compromise, and where Redwood will stand firm. We'll hold off on DocuSign until redlines are resolved.

Oliver / Elena — thanks for the redline and context. We reviewed internally with privacy and product. Summary of Redwood's counter-proposal: 

- Notice: we can commit to 30 days' prior notice for any new subprocessor that will materially process Acme personal data. We'll provide the subprocessor name, location, and a brief description of processing.

- Objection window: we request a 30-day objection window (starting from notice receipt). We believe 15 days is too short for enterprise review plus security assessments; 30 days gives both parties time for operational coordination.

- Relief/remedies: Redwood cannot unilaterally "suspend processing" for a live subprocessor without coordination because that risks availability and patient safety for health customers. Proposed compromise: if Acme objects and the parties cannot reach agreement within the objection window, Redwood will (i) pause onboarding and routing to the new subprocessor for Acme workloads immediately, (ii) continue to route existing traffic through the pre-existing processor(s) while we implement mitigation, and (iii) collaborate on an agreed migration/termination path for the contested processing. If no agreement is reached after 60 days from notice, Acme may elect to terminate the DPA with 30 days' notice solely for the affected scope of processing.

- Evidence: we will provide SOC 2 reports or equivalent evidence within 10 business days where available and are happy to provide additional compliance documentation under NDA for specific subprocessors.

Attached is the current subprocessors list (Redwood_Subprocessors_20250811.csv) for Acme's inventory. If that looks OK, we're prepared to update the DPA with limited carve-outs captured in a short schedule and proceed to DocuSign for execution. We can also mark the subprocessor objection process as an exception in the schedule if that helps.

If acceptable, Karthik — please confirm and I will prepare the execution packet (DocuSign) and the schedule capturing the notice/objection mechanics.

Thanks,
